unit-01-qs: Extensive marine and nonmarine sand deposits, generally near the coast or desert playas.
unit-02-qls: Selected large landslides, such as the Blackhawk Slide on the north side of the San Gabriel Mountains; early to late Quaternary.
unit-03-qrv: Recent (Holocene) volcanic flow rocks; minor pyroclastic deposits.
unit-04-pqrv: Recent (Holocene) pyroclastic and volcanic mudflow deposits.
unit-05-q: Alluvium, lake, playa, and terrace deposits; unconsolidated and semi-consolidated. Mostly nonmarine, but includes marine deposits near the coast.
unit-06-qg: Glacial till and moraines. Found at high elevations mostly in the Sierra Nevada and Klamath Mountains.
unit-07-qv: Quaternary volcanic flow rocks; minor pyroclastic deposits.
unit-08-qvp: Quaternary pyroclastic and volcanic mudflow deposits.
unit-09-qoa: Older alluvium, lake, playa, and terrace deposits.
unit-10-qpc: Pliocene and/or Pleistocene sandstone, shale, and gravel deposits; mostly loosely consolidated.
unit-11-p: Sandstone, siltstone, shale, and conglomerate; mostly moderately consolidated.
unit-12-m: Sandstone, shale, siltstone, conglomerate, and breccia; moderately to well consolidated.
unit-13-mc: Sandstone, shale, conglomerate, and fanglomerate; moderately to well consolidated.
unit-14-tc: Undivided Tertiary sandstone, shale, conglomerate, breccia, and ancient lake deposits.
unit-15-tv: Tertiary volcanic flow rocks; minor pyroclastic deposits.
unit-16-ptv: Tertiary pyroclastic and volcanic mudflow deposits.
unit-17-to: Sandstone, shale, and conglomerate; mostly well consolidated.
unit-18-toc: Sandstone, shale, and conglomerate; mostly well consolidated.
unit-19-e: Shale, sandstone, conglomerate, and minor limestone; mostly well consolidated.
unit-20-ec: Sandstone, shale, and conglomerate; moderately to well consolidated.
unit-21-ti: Tertiary intrusive rocks; mostly shallow (hypabyssal) plugs and dikes.
unit-22-grcz: Cenozoic (Tertiary) granitic rocks—quartz monzonite, quartz latite, and minor monzonite, granodiorite, and granite—found in the Kingston, Panamint, Amargosa, and Greenwater Ranges in southeastern California.
unit-23-ep: Sandstone, shale, and conglomerate; mostly well consolidated.
unit-24-tk: Sandstone, shale, and minor conglomerate in the coastal belt of northwestern California; included by some in the Franciscan Complex. Previously considered Cretaceous, but now known to contain early Tertiary microfossils in places.
unit-25-ku: Upper Cretaceous sandstone, shale, and conglomerate.
unit-26-k: Undivided Cretaceous sandstone, shale, and conglomerate; minor nonmarine rocks in the Peninsular Ranges.
unit-27-grmz: Mesozoic granite, quartz monzonite, granodiorite, and quartz diorite.
unit-28-kl: Lower Cretaceous sandstone, shale, and conglomerate.
unit-29-mzv: Undivided Mesozoic volcanic and metavolcanic rocks. Andesite and rhyolite flow rocks, greenstone, volcanic breccia, and other pyroclastic rocks; in part strongly metamorphosed. Includes volcanic rocks of the Franciscan Complex: basaltic pillow lava, diabase, greenstone, and minor pyroclastic rocks.
unit-30-um: Ultramafic rocks, mostly serpentine. Minor peridotite, gabbro, and diabase; chiefly Mesozoic.
unit-31-kjf: Franciscan Complex: Cretaceous and Jurassic sandstone with smaller amounts of shale, chert, limestone, and conglomerate. Includes Franciscan mélange, except where separated as KJfm.
unit-32-kjfm: Mélange of fragmented and sheared Franciscan Complex rocks.
unit-33-kjfs: Blueschist and semi-schist of the Franciscan Complex.
unit-34-j: Shale, sandstone, minor conglomerate, chert, slate, limestone, and minor pyroclastic rocks.
unit-35-gb: Gabbro and dark dioritic rocks; chiefly Mesozoic.
unit-36-gr-m: Granitic and metamorphic rocks, mostly gneiss and other metamorphic rocks injected by granitic rocks; Mesozoic to Precambrian.
unit-37-tr: Shale, conglomerate, limestone and dolomite, sandstone, slate, hornfels, quartzite, and minor pyroclastic rocks.
unit-38-sch: Schists of various types; mostly Paleozoic or Mesozoic age, with some Precambrian.
unit-40-mv: Undivided pre-Cenozoic metavolcanic rocks. Includes latite, dacite, tuff, and greenstone; commonly schistose.
unit-41-pm: Shale, conglomerate, limestone and dolomite, sandstone, slate, hornfels, quartzite, and minor pyroclastic rocks.
unit-42-m: Undivided pre-Cenozoic metasedimentary and metavolcanic rocks of great variety. Mostly slate, quartzite, hornfels, chert, phyllite, mylonite, schist, gneiss, and minor marble.
unit-43-ls: Limestone, dolomite, and marble whose age is uncertain but probably Paleozoic or Mesozoic.
unit-44-c: Shale, sandstone, conglomerate, limestone, dolomite, chert, hornfels, marble, and quartzite; in part pyroclastic rocks.
unit-45-grpz: Paleozoic and Permo-Triassic granitic rocks in the San Gabriel and Klamath Mountains.
unit-46-pz: Undivided Paleozoic metasedimentary rocks. Includes slate, sandstone, shale, chert, conglomerate, limestone, dolomite, marble, phyllite, schist, hornfels, and quartzite.
unit-47-d: Limestone and dolomite, sandstone, and shale; in part tuffaceous.
unit-48-pzv: Undivided Paleozoic metavolcanic rocks. Mostly flows, breccia, and tuff, including greenstone, diabase, and pillow lavas; minor interbedded sedimentary rocks.
unit-49-so: Sandstone, shale, conglomerate, chert, slate, quartzite, hornfels, marble, dolomite, phyllite, and some greenstone.
unit-50: Sandstone, shale, limestone, dolomite, chert, quartzite, and phyllite; includes some rocks that are possibly Precambrian.
unit-51-p-c: Complex of Precambrian igneous and metamorphic rocks. Mostly gneiss and schist intruded by igneous rocks; may be Mesozoic in part.
unit-52-grp: Precambrian granite, syenite, anorthosite, and gabbroic rocks in the San Gabriel Mountains, plus various Precambrian plutonic rocks elsewhere in southeastern California.
unit-53-p: Conglomerate, shale, sandstone, limestone, dolomite, marble, gneiss, hornfels, and quartzite; may be Paleozoic in part.
